## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `451ada3e886fe7d4c0c4086d160bcd227dc9af70`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/seat-lifecycle.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/state-machine.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/triage-duties.md + scripts/pm/label-write.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs, scripts/pm/close-cards.mjs, scripts/pm/first-touch-sweep.mjs, scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs

Inputs: card #33484 (body, claim comment 6885221965, os-dev-report 6885594065), PR #33510 (body, 10 files, +848 / -29, net diff against main at merge-base b392ff7bdf4), and the check-runs on this head. The PR body's own account was not taken as evidence; every claim below was read in the tree.

Gate verdicts at render (23:19 UTC on the review day): 53 check-runs on this head, 27 success, 26 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. Among them `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Changeset`, `Test Core` (both shards) and every Type Check family: success.

### ① Derived judgments

- `scripts/pm/label-write.mjs`: new refusal (exit 2, step ②, zero writes) on two shapes, on step ①'s own read, before the transport, for the plain write and `--comment-file`. (1) Strip: an OPEN issue loses a `pm:*` state and the target carries none of the six states. (2) Holder: the target sits in `pm:queue` / `pm:blocked` / `pm:on-hold` with an assignee, and the write moved a state or an assignee. New exports: `refuseStatelessWrite`, `PARKED_STATE_LABELS`, `PARKED_RULE`, `STATELESS_RULE_PATH`, `STATELESS_RULE`. This narrows what an internal CLI accepts, which is right per card item 1. The legal exits are another state, `needs-user-decision`, a close, the ONE-OF repair, a pull request, a closed card, or a write that moves neither a state nor an assignee (a regrade). All are right and all are pinned. The self-test's `raced` case moved from a lone `pm:queue` removal to `skip-changeset`, because the lone strip is now refused. That is right: the DELETE race is still driven, so nothing was weakened. Battery +19 and floor 15 to 16: right.
- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`: actions files gain a new exit 2 (refused) and exit 3 (unreadable card). A dry run now needs a token when the stroke strips or parks a card, which is the same shape as the kind rule: right. `readLabelTargetKinds` takes an optional `cache`, backward-compatible, so there is one GET per card shared with the guard. Right: both readers store the same `rest()` answer keyed by the action's `issue`. New exports: `STATE_GUARD_OPS`, `stateGuardRows`, `judgeStateGuard`, `readStateGuard`. The `cliQuiet` fixture moved from `pm:queue` to `pm:awaiting-merge` so that its zero-reads case stays zero reads. That is right: `pm:awaiting-merge` is not one of the six states.
- `scripts/pm/close-cards.mjs`: `packCard` refuses a pack whose stroke strips without closing. Every pack built there closes, so the refusal is a pin and not a new behaviour: right.
- `scripts/pm/first-touch-sweep.mjs`: a new report-only CLI with exits 0 / 2 / 3 / 4 and no writes. Right.
- `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`: four ceilings raised. Each is measured against the tree: state-machine 41 to 43 (+2 -0), landing-operations 107 to 108 (+3 -2), seat-lifecycle 98 to 99 (+1), triage-duties 101 to 103 (+3 -1). SKILL.md stays at 319 lines (+2 -2), and its ceiling did not move. Each ceiling moved by exactly the lines added, and each comment cites the ruling quoted in the card body and claim comment 6885221965. Right.
- Nothing under `packages/**` or another published surface moves.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is on the PR and no changeset is in the diff. The diff touches only `scripts/pm/**` and `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**`, and neither is published. `Check Changeset` is success. That matches. `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and claim is right: no published schema or accept set is in the diff. The narrowed accept sets are internal PM tools, and the governed register puts this PR on the rules face, not the narrowing face.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question (do done-and-gated `pm:blocked` cards keep their holder?): the seat answered A, so the card's rule stands and no parked state keeps an assignee. The diff conforms to A: the SKILL.md row adds `pm:blocked`/`pm:on-hold` to 「`pm:queue` 卡恒无 assignee,有即半态」, and `PARKED_STATE_LABELS` holds all three with no carve-out. Settled.
- Out-of-scope (1), the sweep's self-test is not run by CI: confirmed. No workflow runs the script, so `check-self-test-wired` is silent. I checked by `git show` that each of the eight `TRIAGE_RULE_PHRASES`, the multi-lane phrase and `PARKED_RULE` is a substring of its rule file at this head. Disposition: a follow-up card (see N7). It is noted on the report but not filed, so the seat files it.
- Out-of-scope (2), the four ruled ratchet raises: judged in ①, all right. The signature under `Fixes` instead of line 1: accepted, and `PR-body guards` is success. The MANDATORY tier and GOVERNED Tier S readings: this record is the owed review.
- `Restart-grade` regrades of #27124, #27287 and #32481 stay with triage after landing, as the order says. No card was relabelled by the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**Rules faces (hits).**

- `state-machine.md`: 「开着的卡离手恒落一态:摘 `pm:*` 态同笔补下一态、`needs-user-decision` 或关卡;写门拒半写」 is card item 1 word for word, and `STATELESS_RULE` quotes it. The hold line (`priority:p3` in the same stroke, ` · Restart-grade: pN` at the end of the `Restart-when:` line, restored on restart, trackers and epics the same) is card item 3. I read `classifyRestartWhen` on main. The appended suffix keeps `closed-ref`, `issue-ref` and a backticked `command` fireable, so H9 and the unlock sweep are unaffected (see N5 for the bare-head command case).
- `SKILL.md`: the queue row keeps 「`pm:queue` 卡恒无 assignee,有即半态」 verbatim. That phrase is what H24 in `check-half-states.mjs` quotes, and the second commit restored it. The parked states are appended, and the `pm:on-hold` row names the p3 drop. Both hold against the card. See N4 (no detector for the new half-state) and N6 (the human floor).
- `landing-operations.md`: the three lines answer the old line's gap (收口 without saying what to). Item 2 is met: the remainder gets a state for its lane (`pm:queue` with its `domain:*`, re-domained across lanes; `pm:blocked` with `Blocked-by:`; hold with `Restart-when:`), the assignee is cleared, and a comment says what was delivered and who owns the rest.
- `seat-lifecycle.md`: the stay-behind state is set in the `seat-offline` stroke, or by triage in the round it reads that knock. This is item 2's second half, and it stays consistent with 「离任留守只写点名的…PR」.
- `triage-duties.md`: the 「待维护者」 list now names every `needs-user-decision` and `pm:awaiting-maintainer` card with its age (item 5). The sweep line names the script and forbids narrowing (item 4). The self-repair line takes the p3 drop (item 3).

**Implementing files.**

- `refuseStatelessWrite` was driven against the brief's break list:
  - A lone `--remove pm:dispatched` is refused, end to end, with zero writes.
  - A case-varied `PM:Dispatched` is refused.
  - `--release` passes. It is legal by construction (`pm:dispatched` to `pm:queue`, every assignee cleared), but see N1.
  - A close passes, and an already-closed card is never judged.
  - `pm:dispatched` to `needs-user-decision` with the holder kept passes, because the target is not parked.
  - The state swaps pass: `pm:dispatched` to `pm:queue` with `--clear-assignees`, and `pm:queue` to `pm:dispatched` with an assign (the claim).
  - Parking with the holder kept is refused, by design under A.
  - A hold regrade with an old assignee passes, because it moves no state and no assignee.
  - Clearing a stale assignee from a `pm:queue` card passes.
- The strip half has no bypass through `issue_patch`: `validate.mjs` admits only title, body, state and state_reason there. A removal of `needs-user-decision` that leaves a card stateless passes, which is the rule as written (it names `pm:*`); the sweep's ① and ③ backstop it.
- `dispatch.mjs` `stateGuardRows` / `judgeStateGuard` apply the stroke's steps in order and ask label-write's predicate rather than restating it. One hole remains (S1).
- In `first-touch-sweep.mjs`, the five disjunctions match `triage-duties.md`:
  - ①: no `pm:*`, no `needs-user-decision`, no `domain:*` (a bare `finding` hits).
  - ②: `pm:queue` without `domain:*`, multi-lane board only.
  - ③: `domain:*` and none of the six states.
  - ④: `pm:queue` with `domain:*` and no `priority:*`.
  - ②③④ apply only to cards settled for 2 minutes. The exclusions come first, and ⑤ is read from label events, never by actor.
- The walk reads every page until a short page, with a ceiling of 60 pages, and drops pull requests. It compares `total_count` and `incomplete_results` and exits 4 `INCOMPLETE` on any gap. A ⑤ card whose events cannot be read makes the run INCOMPLETE. All of this matches the card. See S2, N2 and N3.

**Findings.**

- **S1 · should-fix** (`scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`, `stateGuardRows`): an `assign`-only relay stroke onto a card parked in `pm:queue`, `pm:blocked` or `pm:on-hold` is never read, so the holder half passes at the relay door. label-write refuses the same write, and its own self-test pins 「assigning a card that sits in pm:queue is REFUSED too」. Card item 1 names the fleet-write path for the holder rule, and label-write's header calls the predicate 「the ONE predicate, asked … at every door」. Fix: mark the row judged on `assign` as well, so that the claim stroke still passes (it strips `pm:queue`). Add one self-test case each way.
- **S2 · should-fix** (`scripts/pm/first-touch-sweep.mjs`, `verdictLine`): without `--since`, ⑤ is skipped, yet the run prints `sweep CLEAN — no card owed a first touch (⑤ NOT RUN: no --since window)` and exits 0. The file's own header says 「without `--since` it is NOT RUN and the verdict says so — ⛔ never clean」, and the card's point is that no disjunction is narrowed. A patrol that drops the flag reads CLEAN on four disjunctions. Fix: a verdict word that is not CLEAN (for example `sweep PARTIAL`) and an exit that is not 0, or refuse to run without `--since`. Pin it with a self-test case.
- **N1 · nit** (`scripts/pm/label-write.mjs` header and the PR body): both say the predicate is asked for 「the plain write, `--comment-file` and `--release` alike」, but `runRelease` never calls `refuseStatelessWrite`. A release is legal by construction and the predicate-level pin covers it, so nothing breaks. Correct the sentence, or ask the predicate in `runRelease` too. Accepted deviation.
- **N2 · nit** (sweep walk): pages are read by offset in the endpoint's default created-descending order. A card closed between two page reads shifts a still-open card across the boundary. That card is missed while the counts still agree (both N-1), and the run reads complete. The window is seconds wide and the next fire catches it. Dedupe by number and walk created-ascending as a follow-up.
- **N3 · nit** (sweep ⑤): `fifthCandidate` prefilters on the labels the card carries now. A card whose creation-minute `pm:queue` or `priority:*` has since come off is never judged, and the rule text has no current-label clause. Harmless in practice, because such a card has been touched since. Follow-up or accepted.
- **N4 · nit** (`SKILL.md` queue row): `pm:blocked`/`pm:on-hold` with an assignee is now declared 有即半态, but H24 in `check-half-states.mjs` reads `pm:queue` only. The 2 of 24 `pm:blocked` cards with an assignee that the report names stay invisible to the half-state patrol until a write moves their state. The write door covers new writes. Follow-up card: widen H24 to the three parked states. Triage repairs the two cards.
- **N5 · nit** (`state-machine.md` hold line): appending ` · Restart-grade: pN` to a bare-head command value (`Restart-when: pnpm …`) means the line no longer runs verbatim as the 「一行可执行判据」 the hold rule requires. The classifier is unaffected. The placement is the card's own, so it is an accepted deviation. A prose follow-up could backtick a command value when the grade is appended.
- **N6 · nit** (`triage-duties.md` human floor): the floor lists 「卡的命运(关 not planned、降级、撤回、砍半)」, while the new hold rule lowers a card to p3 in the same stroke, including a seat-graded hold. The maintainer's ruling on the card makes it 「既裁执行」, but the text does not say so, so a seat may present each hold regrade. Accepted, or a one-clause prose follow-up.
- **N7 · nit** (follow-up): wire `first-touch-sweep.mjs --self-test` into CI (a root alias and a `lint.yml` step, Tier H). Until then its phrase pin against `triage-duties.md` runs nowhere automatically. File the card the report left unfiled.

No must-fix. S1 and S2 each earn a delta review of their fix. The nits stand as listed.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-milihp`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5pjSPT7ui2EUcunaVb`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d00151d4ad4742222d02e5a7ed9e233f38e530b5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/seat-lifecycle.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/state-machine.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/triage-duties.md + scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs, scripts/pm/first-touch-sweep.mjs, scripts/pm/label-write.mjs

Delta review. The earlier record is PR #33510 comment 6885812549, a PASS on head `451ada3e886fe7d4c0c4086d160bcd227dc9af70` with two should-fix findings (S1, S2) and seven nits (N1 to N7). This record judges fix commit d00151d4 on top of it.

Inputs: comment 6885812549; card #33484 (body, claim comment 6885221965, os-dev-report 6885594065); PR #33510 (body, 10 files, +874 / -29); `git diff 451ada3e886fe7d4c0c4086d160bcd227dc9af70 d00151d4ad4742222d02e5a7ed9e233f38e530b5` (3 files, +52 / -26: `first-touch-sweep.mjs`, `fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`, `label-write.mjs`); and the check-runs on this head. Every new line of the delta was read. Neither the PR body's account of the fix nor the dev's was taken as evidence.

Gate verdicts at render (23:54 UTC on the review day): 48 check-runs on this head, 26 success, 22 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. These include `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` (which runs the label-write, fleet-write dispatch and close-cards self-tests), `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, both `PR-body guards` runs, `Test Core` (both shards and the rollup), and every Type Check family: all success. Both `Check Changeset` runs are skipped, which is the `skip-changeset` path.

### Delta

- **S1 · fixed.** `stateGuardRows` (`dispatch.mjs` L1118) now judges a card when the stroke runs `assign` with at least one login. `judgeStateGuard` applies every step and then asks `refuseStatelessWrite` about the final label and assignee sets, so step order does not matter. I tried to break it:
  - An assign-only stroke onto `pm:queue`, `pm:blocked` or `pm:on-hold` is refused with label-write's `PARKED_RULE` sentence. It costs one GET and sends nothing, and the new CLI case pins this for `pm:queue`.
  - Legal strokes still pass. An assign onto `pm:dispatched` packs on one GET (pinned). The claim stroke (`pm:queue` off, `pm:dispatched` on, plus the assign) passes in any order, because the final set has no parked state. It was already read through its `labels_remove`, so it costs no new GET. An assign onto a closed card, a pull request or a `needs-user-decision` card passes on the predicate's own exits. An assign in a stroke that closes its card reads nothing.
  - An `unassign` and an empty `assign` read nothing. An assign whose login is already on the card moves nothing and passes, the same as label-write.
  - No GET is added where none is owed. Only the read can tell whether the card is already parked, so the GET is owed, and it shares the kind rule's `cardReads` cache. label-write's own assigns go through `sendFleetWrite` rather than this `main`, so they gain no second read. `close-cards.mjs` packs always close, so its `stateGuardRows` refusal still never fires.
  - The rows pin that used an `assign` to show "touches no state" now uses `unassign`. The `assign` case moved to its own expectation (`[5]`), so no coverage was lost. Battery 6 to 8.
- **S2 · fixed.** `verdictLine` without `--since` now prints `sweep PARTIAL — ⑤ NOT RUN …`, and the new `sweepExit` returns 0 only when `complete && fifthRun`, otherwise 4. `main` returns `sweepExit(r)`. The header, the exit table and USAGE all name PARTIAL as exit 4, and all three agree with the code. `renderJson` carries the same verdict string and `fifth_run`. A `--since` later than now is still refused as usage (exit 2), so a future window cannot buy a vacuous CLEAN. `triage-duties.md` already names `--since=ISO` on the sweep line. Pinned: the empty board exits 0 with `--since` and 4 without it, and the verdict starts `sweep PARTIAL`. The walk battery's FOUND case is now the PARTIAL case. CLI battery 7 to 9, total 45.
- **N1 · fixed.** `runRelease` now asks `refuseStatelessWrite` at step ② (`label-write.mjs` L1634). It uses the card read at step ①, the release's label target (`pm:queue`) and its assignee target, which is empty because of `clearAll`. So it passes, and the header's 「the plain write, `--comment-file` and `--release` alike」 is now true. The existing release drives that exit 0 run through the new call, so a refusal there would turn the self-test red. See N10 for the pin.
- **N2 · not fixed** (offset paging can miss a card when the board shifts mid-walk). Outside the delta. It stands as a follow-up.
- **N3 · not fixed** (⑤ prefilters on the labels the card carries now). Outside the delta. It stands as a follow-up or an accepted deviation.
- **N4 · not fixed** (H24 reads `pm:queue` only). Outside the delta. It stands as a follow-up card.
- **N5 · not fixed** (the `Restart-grade` suffix on a command value with a bare head). Outside the delta. It stands as an accepted deviation.
- **N6 · not fixed** (the human-floor wording for a hold regrade). Outside the delta. It stands as accepted.
- **N7 · not fixed** (the sweep self-test is not wired into CI). The PR body's acceptance notes still carry it, and the follow-up card is still owed by the seat.

### ① Derived judgments

- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`: an actions file with an `assign` onto a card that is not closed in the same stroke now needs a card read. That adds two new outcomes for such a file: exit 2 when the card is parked, and exit 3 when it cannot be read. A dry run of that file without a token is now exit 3. This narrows an internal CLI's accept set to match label-write's: right, and it is S1's own ask. The new import is `PARKED_RULE`. No export was removed.
- `scripts/pm/first-touch-sweep.mjs`: a run without `--since` moves from exit 0 to exit 4. A patrol that drops the flag now reads a failure: right, and it is S2's own ask. New export: `sweepExit`.
- `scripts/pm/label-write.mjs`: `--release` gains a step ② check that the release shape always passes. No accept-set change.
- The `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**` hits are unchanged by the delta. The rules-face judgment in the earlier record stands.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset`. The delta touches only `scripts/pm/**`, which is not published. Both `Check Changeset` runs are skipped on this head, which is the labelled path. `Clause-②: no` still holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No new boundary. The delta stays inside the order's surface (`scripts/pm/**`), and no card was relabelled.
- Tier S (`.claude/**` paths in the PR), so this record is what the seat lands on.
- Option A (no parked state keeps a holder) is unchanged, and S1 extends it to the relay door. Settled.

### ④ Design judgment

Every new line of the delta was read. The fixes take the shape the earlier record asked for. The relay door asks the one predicate rather than restating it, and the sweep has a verdict word and an exit that a patrol cannot misread as clean. Findings on the new lines:

- **N8 · nit** (`dispatch.mjs` L4688, the no-token prerequisite sentence): the header, the `stateGuardRows` doc and the unread sentence in `readStateGuard` now say 「parks it or assigns someone to it」. The token-missing branch in `main` still says 「the stroke takes a pm state off card N or parks it」. An assign-only dry run with no token therefore gets a reason that does not describe its stroke. The exit (3) is right; only the reason is wrong. Fix: add 「or assigns someone to it」.
- **N9 · nit** (`dispatch.mjs` stateless-door battery): the claim stroke (`pm:queue` off, `pm:dispatched` on, plus an assign) is the legal assign onto a parked card. It passes at the relay door, as read above, but is pinned only at label-write's predicate, not through the door's `cli`. Add one case so a later change to the row picker cannot refuse a claim unseen.
- **N10 · nit** (`label-write.mjs` STATELESS battery): the new runRelease pin brings the battery to 20 cases, but its floor stays 19, so the pin can be deleted without turning anything red. dispatch (6 to 8) and the sweep (7 to 9) raised their floors. The pin is also a source-text check (`String(fn).includes('refuseStatelessWrite(')`). It is backed behaviourally only because the release drives pass through the call. Raise the floor to 20.
- **N11 · nit** (outside the delta; follow-up): the holder half judges assign, label and release strokes. A card created open with `pm:queue` (or another parked state) and an assignee in one write is judged by no door: the relay's `issue_create` op and `issue-create.mjs --label … --assignee …` both accept it. Nothing files cards that way today, and H24 sees a `pm:queue` holder afterwards. File a follow-up card to ask the predicate of a create as well.

No must-fix and no should-fix. S1, S2 and N1 are fixed. N2 to N7 stand as the earlier record listed them. N8 to N11 are nits, so this round ends here.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
